title: On a shared front-desk computer, gym alerts follow only the last person who turned them on, and go silent when that person signs out
what: One computer can hold alerts for only one sign-in. If the owner turns alerts on and later the desk turns them on in the same browser, the owner's alerts there are quietly replaced by the desk's smaller set. When the desk then signs out, that computer gets no alerts at all, though the owner turned them on there. Turning alerts off for one person also switches them off for everyone on that browser. Nobody is told; it only shows as off if someone opens the alerts card again.
expected: A shared computer keeps alerts for each person who turned them on, or at least says plainly that alerts on this computer now belong to the desk and warns when signing out will stop them.
who: owners and front desk sharing one computer
how_often: every time two people use the same browser
fix_line: Let one browser keep alerts for each sign-in, or warn on the alerts card and at sign-out

title: When the browser renews its alert address, gym alerts stop with no warning
what: Browsers sometimes replace the address alerts are sent to. The admin app's background helper does not catch that, so the gym server keeps sending to the old address and the owner stops getting alerts with the app closed. The alerts card shows Off only if someone opens it again.
expected: The new address is saved by itself, or the admin app says alerts on this device stopped and asks to turn them on again the next time it opens.
who: owners and staff with alerts on
fix_line: Save the renewed address in the background helper, and warn on opening when it no longer matches

title: A shop order marked ready by mistake and put back to new still tells the member it is ready, and marking it ready again sends nothing
what: Marking an order Ready sends the member 'Your order is ready. Collect it at the desk.' If the desk puts it back to New, that pop-up is never taken back. When the order really is ready later, no second pop-up goes, because the first one already used up the order's one ready message.
expected: Putting an order back to New removes the ready note, and a later Ready tells the member again.
who: members who order in the app
how_often: only when an order is put back to new
fix_line: Clear the ready note on back-to-new and allow a fresh one on the next Ready
